children.label: Add Plant
children.desc: Grow a new plant at the 3D cursor, from the Rudbeckia fulgida preset. Select it later to change it

children.label: Regrow
children.desc: Rebuild the active plant with its current settings. The stems come back unwelded unless this exact plant was welded before -- welding is the Weld button

children.label: Live Update
children.name: Live Update
children.desc: Regrow automatically a moment after changing a value, instead of only on the Regrow button

children.label: Master Seed
children.name: Seed
children.desc: Master seed: changes the individual plant without changing the species, every level's and component's own Seed mixed with it. The same seeds and settings always grow the same plant

children.label: Species Presets
children.desc: The species preset Library -- bundled presets first, then the user's own, then Load-from-file for a preset that lives outside either folder. Each entry applies onto the active plant. Scanning the folders happens here, on open, not in the panel draw -- so the panel stays free of disk I/O.

children.label: Day
children.name: Day
children.desc: The day to grow the plant to, counting from day 0. Unbounded - a perennial lives many years, so this runs past 365 into later seasons. Whole days here, but float-typed so the smooth timelapse can drive fractional days later. A calendar month/year view is a display of this

children.label: Open Phenology Calendar
children.desc: Open a calendar to author the plant's bloom / fruit / autumn timing by dragging, and scrub the Day. Click again to close

children.label: Lifespan
children.name: Lifespan
children.desc: How the plant lives across years. Only affects Days scrubbed past the first season -- the mature Day-270 view is the same for all three
items: One season that stays mature past its end -- the original behaviour. Nothing changes when the Day is scrubbed into a later year
Lives one season, then dies at season end (fully senesced, standing) and never comes back
Dies back to bare ground each winter and regrows a fresh top each spring, a touch bigger year over year to a mature plateau

children.label: Grow Over Timeline
children.name: Grow Over Timeline
children.desc: Play this plant's growth on the timeline: every frame sets the Day (Start Day on the scene's first frame, End Day on its last) and regrows the real plant. Exact -- every stem, leaf and flower as it is on that day -- but a full regrow per frame, so it is for rendering a growth timelapse, not for real-time playback. While on, the Day field follows the timeline

children.label: Start Day
children.name: Start Day
children.desc: The Day the growth timelapse shows on the scene's first frame

children.label: End Day
children.name: End Day
children.desc: The Day the growth timelapse shows on the scene's last frame. Past a perennial's first season this runs into dormancy and next year's regrowth

children.label: Bake Timelapse
children.desc: Grow every frame of the timeline once and record it, so Grow Over Timeline plays back smoothly (frames already recorded are skipped). Esc stops; the frames done so far are kept

children.label: Layout
children.name: Layout
items: One row of plants, one parameter stepped along it
Rows of rows: a second parameter (or only the seeds) varies from row to row

children.label: Plants
children.name: Plants
children.desc: Plants in a row

children.label: Seed Step
children.name: Seed Step
children.desc: The gap between the plants' seeds: the plant's Seed + this, + twice this, ... (Step 100 on Seed 0: 100, 200, 300...). Change it for a fresh set

children.label: Day
children.desc: Pick the parameter to step: search it by name

children.label: Start
children.name: Start
children.desc: Its value at the first plant of a row

children.label: Step
children.name: Step
children.desc: Added at each next plant along a row

children.label: Auto Spacing
children.name: Auto Spacing
children.desc: Space plants by the widest one's footprint, a quarter to spare

children.label: Spacing X
children.name: Spacing X
children.desc: Distance between plants in a row

children.label: Labels
children.name: Labels
children.desc: A caption under each plant: its values and seed

children.label: Weld
children.name: Weld
children.desc: Weld every plant's junctions as it is built (slow). Off: the quick unwelded preview; Bake welds anyway

children.label: Build Variations
children.desc:
Build (or rebuild) this plant's variations from its current settings: a row
or grid of copies, each its own seed, the chosen parameters stepped across
them. The old set is replaced

children.label: Bake to Meshes
children.desc:
Bake every variation to one plain mesh object (welded, leaves and flowers
realized, no modifiers), in its own collection. The live variations are hidden

children.label: Clear
children.desc: Delete this plant's variations (their plants and labels). Baked meshes stay

children.label: Export Nanite Assembly
children.desc:
Export this plant and its variations as one USD file of Nanite Assemblies
for Unreal 5.7+. Imported from one file, they share their leaf and flower
meshes, materials and textures. Beside it, one wind JSON per plant. A plant
with no current rig gets one for the export

children.label: Add Flower
children.desc: Create a new standalone flower in its own Collection. Select any flower later to edit it

children.label: Save Flower Preset
children.desc: Save the active flower's settings as a .json preset

children.label: Load Flower Preset
children.desc: Load a .json preset onto the active flower

children.label: Add To Pool
children.desc: Toggle whether this flower's main object is in the shared PlantGen_FlowerAssets Collection (created on first use), where baked bloom stages also land -- a collection a flower component can draw on. Depressed when already in the pool; click again to remove it

children.label: Bake To Mesh
children.desc: Freeze the active/selected flower(s) into a single static Mesh object each, with no modifiers, properties, or Sepals/Disc/Receptacle children -- in the shared baked-assets collection, for when you want a lightweight, no-longer-editable asset. Runs on every selected flower, not just the active one; the flowers themselves are left untouched

children.label: Seed
children.name: Seed
children.desc: Random seed for variance

children.label: Bloom
children.name: Bloom
children.desc: Open the flower (1) or close it into a bud (0). Blends each whorl's own Bud Curl in underneath its authored open-pose Curl Up/Down -- Bloom rising IS the petals/sepals physically uncurling. Each whorl maps this through its own Bloom Start/End window (see Bud under Petals/Sepals), so petals and sepals close/open together while opening on their own schedule. Keyframe it for a bud-to-bloom animation. 0 here is remapped internally onto the best-looking closed pose found by testing (not literally zero bend) -- see blender/flower.py's _BLOOM_UI_FLOOR

children.label: Maturity
children.name: Maturity
children.desc: Global development/size 'time' for the whole flower, shaped by the Maturity Scale profile into an overall size multiplier -- independent of Bloom (how open it is) and of per-layer Age

children.label: Stages
children.name: Bloom Stages
children.desc: How many fixed-Bloom copies "Bake Bloom Stages" creates, evenly spaced from fully closed to fully open

children.label: Stages Variance
children.name: Bloom Stages Variance
children.desc: Random +/- jitter applied to each stage's evenly-spaced Bloom value (re-rolled by Seed above), so stages land close to but not exactly on an even split

children.label: Bake Bloom Stages
children.desc: Create several fixed-Bloom copies of the active/selected flower(s) (e.g. bud/half-open/full-bloom, per each one's own Bloom Stages/Variance fields), named bud to open, into the shared pool collection: point a flower component's Collection at them and each flower shows the stage its own openness calls for. Runs on every selected flower, not just the active one

children.label: Enable
children.name: Enable
children.desc: Generate petals

children.label: Presets
children.desc: 'Presets' dropdown in the Petals box's Corolla Type row -- one click sets a whole named botanical corolla form (Cruciform/Tubular/etc, see `flower_ops.FLOWER_COROLLA_PRESETS`) at once, instead of hand-tuning Count/ Fusion/Width or Fusion Profile separately. Mirrors `ui.py`'s `PLANTGEN_MT_flower_position_presets` flat-list style, just for a flower's own SHAPE (`obj.plantgen_flower`) instead of its placement on a stem -- lives here rather than in `ui.py` for that reason. Label-matching (`_matching_corolla_label`) mirrors the position presets' own dropdown button, same "most-specific match wins" rule.

children.label: Presets
children.desc: 'Presets' dropdown in the Petals box's Petal Shape row -- one click sets a named botanical outline (Ovate/Obovate/Spatulate/etc, see `flower_ops.FLOWER_PETAL_SHAPES`), meaning BOTH the Width Profile that shapes the sides and the Top Shape cap that finishes the tip.

children.label: Resolution
children.name: Resolution
children.desc: Points along each petal's spine

children.label: Width Resolution
children.name: Width Resolution
children.desc: Points across each petal (Resolution is along it). With Fuse To Tube on, the tube is revolved with Count x (this - 1) sides to weld to it

children.label: Flip Normals
children.name: Flip Normals
children.desc: Turn the petals' faces the other way round (the front becomes the back)

children.label: Length
children.name: Length
children.desc: Petal length from the disc edge to its tip

children.label: Width
children.name: Width
children.desc: Full petal width at the Width Profile curve's peak

children.label: Top Shape
children.name: Top Shape
children.desc: Shapes the petal's TIP cap edge, using the Top Shape curve as a profile across the petal's WIDTH -- a different axis from the Width Profile, which shapes the sides along its LENGTH. Measured in multiples of the tip's own width, so a Dome curve at 0.5 is a semicircular tip at any petal size; negative notches the cap inward instead. 0 leaves the flat, straight-cut tip

children.label: Bottom Shape
children.name: Bottom Shape
children.desc: Shapes the petal's BASE cap edge, same units and curve convention as Top Shape. Added ON TOP of the automatic fit that already curves the base to match whatever it attaches to (the disc rim, or a corolla tube's mouth), so 0 is not a flat cut here -- it's the shape that meets that surface cleanly

children.label: Cup
children.name: Cup
children.desc: Bows the petal's CROSS-SECTION (across the width, not along its length) into a shallow channel/dome, as a real distance push scaled by the ring's own local width -- fades to 0 wherever the petal itself tapers to nothing (the tip, and a narrow base). One shared value for every petal on this flower, not per-petal like the fields above

children.label: Scale
children.name: Scale
children.desc: Overall size multiplier (scales Length and Width together), shaped across layers by its own Age Profile curve -- e.g. lets the topmost/innermost layer read as younger and smaller

children.label: Count
children.name: Count
children.desc: Number of petals per layer, evenly spaced around the disc

children.label: Radial Offset
children.name: Radial Offset
children.desc: Signed distance moving each petal's BASE along the disc's own radius. Positive pulls it inward, toward the disc's axis; negative pushes it OUTWARD instead, past the disc rim, like a pedicel -- same convention as Leaves/Flowers' own Radial Offset on a stem. This is a deliberate placement offset, NOT a seam fix: the base cap is already fitted to whatever it attaches to automatically, so 0 should look correct on its own

children.label: Vertical Offset
children.name: Vertical Offset
children.desc: Signed Z distance moving each petal's BASE up(+) or down(-) -- lets the base meet a Fusion tube's own rim, or the Disc's surface, exactly when Curvature/Pitch differences leave a visible gap or overlap there

children.label: Spread Horizontal
children.name: Spread Horizontal
children.desc: Random scatter of each petal's BASE azimuth around its ideal evenly-spaced ring position -- unlike Yaw (under Shape), this moves WHERE the base sits rather than which way it points

children.label: Clamp Overlap
children.name: Clamp Overlap
children.desc: Limits how wide neighbouring petals may get before they meet. 0 is off -- they overlap freely, which many real polypetalous flowers do. 1 makes their edges land exactly on each other, with no gap and no intersection. Below 1 allows proportionally more overlap; above 1 pulls them narrower than touching, opening a deliberate gap between petals. Applied along the whole length, not just at the base -- the room available widens as the petal reaches further from the axis

children.label: Layers
children.name: Layers
children.desc: Number of stacked petal rings (whorls), each offset up/down by Spacing and rotated by Spiral from the last -- a double-flower / many-petaled look. 1 = a single ring

children.label: Spacing
children.name: Spacing
children.desc: Vertical distance between successive petal layers -- typically well under 1mm

children.label: Spiral
children.name: Spiral
children.desc: Azimuthal rotation applied to each successive layer, so layers interleave instead of stacking directly on top of each other. Defaults to the golden angle (~137.5°), the same botanical spiral stems use for Golden phyllotaxis

children.label: Gravity
children.name: Gravity
children.desc: Bends each petal toward world-up (+) or world-down (-), shaped by the Gravity profile curve. Settles at vertical and can't overshoot past it, however high the value

children.label: Twist
children.name: Twist
children.desc: Total rotation of the petal's cross-section around its own spine, shaped by the Twist profile curve; doesn't bend the spine itself. 1.0 = 180°, independent of Length

children.label: Up/Down
children.name: Curl Up/Down
children.desc: Steady bend up (+) or down (-) out of the flat disc plane, shaped along the petal by its own profile curve. 1.0 = 180° total, independent of Length -- keeps coiling tighter the higher you push it, no clamp (unlike Gravity)

children.label: Left/Right
children.name: Curl Left/Right
children.desc: Steady sideways bend, curving the petal into a sickle/scimitar shape as it extends outward. 1.0 = 180° total, independent of Length

children.label: Out/In
children.name: Curl Out/In
children.desc: Corkscrews the petal's lean around the disc's own central (world Z) axis. 1.0 = 180° total, independent of Length

children.label: Roll
children.name: Curl Roll
children.desc: Redirects which plane Curl Up/Down and Gravity bend the petal in -- doesn't move a flat petal by itself. A second, independent Roll from Rotation's own (which instead spins the already-built cross-section, visible even at zero Curl)

children.label: Yaw
children.name: Yaw
children.desc: One-time rotation of each petal's pointing direction around the disc's own normal, independent of where its base attaches (which stays evenly spaced on the rim) -- fans petals unevenly for an overlapping, pinwheel look. Positive Variance alone is often enough

children.label: Pitch
children.name: Pitch
children.desc: One-time tilt of each petal's starting direction up/down out of the flat disc plane, before any Curl/Gravity bending is applied on top

children.label: Roll
children.name: Roll
children.desc: Spins the petal's cross-section around its own local direction (length) axis, sideways -- visible along the whole petal, including the base, even with zero Curl/Twist

children.label: Curl Up/Down
children.name: Bud Curl
children.desc: Extra Curl Up/Down bend fully applied when this whorl's own local Bloom is 0, fading to zero extra (i.e. exactly Curl Up/Down above) as it opens -- Bloom rising IS this uncurling. Now that Bud Pitch (above) carries most of the closing motion, keep this small (well under 0.3 with the default Bud Curl Profile) -- much higher and the bend overshoots 180 degrees, so the tip swings past vertical and back toward/through the axis as it starts to relax, reading as the tip pulling back before it unfurls outward. The Tip Shape controls below are the actual pointed-vs-round lever now, so Bud Curl only needs to add a little extra curve on top of the hinge

children.label: Rotation Pitch
children.name: Bud Pitch
children.desc: EXPERIMENTAL: this whorl's Rotation Pitch at local Bloom 0 (near-vertical, closed), fading to the authored open-pose Pitch above as it opens -- a rigid hinge swing from pointing up to pointing out, which is how a real flower's bloom reads mostly (~70-80%), with Curl only providing a minor unfurl (~20-30%) on top. Unlike Curl, a rigid rotation from vertical can't wrap past itself, so this is inherently monotonic regardless of angle

children.label: Radial Offset
children.name: Bud Sink
children.desc: Radial pull on each petal's own BASE toward the disc axis, fully applied at local Bloom 0, fading to zero extra (i.e. exactly Radial Offset) as it opens. Curl alone converges each petal's TIP to a point but leaves its base at the full open-flower radius, which still reads as a wide spiky crown rather than a slender bud -- this presses the bases together near the axis too

children.label: Cup
children.name: Bud Cup
children.desc: This whorl's Cup at local Bloom 0 (closed), fading to the authored open-pose Cup above as it opens -- the same true-pair pattern as Bud Pitch/Bud Curl/Bud Sink. The same cross-section cup reads flatter once everything's pinched down toward the axis, so the bud pose typically wants noticeably MORE cup than the open pose to still read as cupped -- authored independently here rather than derived from it

children.label: Clamp Overlap
children.name: Bud Clamp Overlap
children.desc: This whorl's own Clamp Overlap at local Bloom 0 (closed), fading to the authored open-pose Clamp Overlap (under Shape) as it opens. Bud Sink above already pulls every base toward the axis as the whorl closes, which shrinks the touching-width ceiling Clamp Overlap measures against -- without its own bud value, widths authored for the open radius can pile up and cover the axis instead of reading as separate furled petals. 0 = off (matches the open default)

children.label: Start
children.name: Bloom Start
children.desc: Bloom value below which this whorl is fully closed (local bloom 0). Defaults to 0.44 -- 80% of the way through Sepals' own Bloom End (0.55) -- so petals stay closed until the calyx is nearly done opening, then follow

children.label: End
children.name: Bloom End
children.desc: Bloom value above which this whorl is fully open (local bloom 1) -- a narrower window than the sibling whorl's makes this one finish opening earlier

children.label: Tip Zone Start
children.name: Tip Zone Start
children.desc: Where along the petal (0=base, 1=tip) the tip-shaping zone starts. Height/Radius profiles below are evaluated across just this zone (0 here -> 1 at the tip), so they always get full curve resolution regardless of where the zone starts

children.label: Tip Pointiness
children.name: Bud Tip Lift
children.desc: Overall height magnitude raised into the tip zone (shaped by the Height profile below), fully applied at local Bloom 0, fading to zero as it opens. Curl alone always rounds the apex off into a dome (a constant-curvature arc); this pinches it up past that arc. 0 = off

children.label: Tip Falloff
children.name: Tip Falloff
children.desc: How fast tip shaping releases as this whorl opens: tip_fade = (1 - local Bloom) ^ this. 1.0 = plain linear release across the same range Curl itself unwinds over; higher values front-load the release (most of it happens early) while still easing smoothly to exactly 0 at fully open -- no separate cutoff point to desync from Curl's own pace

children.label: Enable
children.name: Enable
children.desc: Generate a shared corolla tube the petal lobes emerge from (Sympetalous/Gamopetalous)

children.label: Length
children.name: Length
children.desc: Length of the corolla tube, independent of Petal Length (the free lobe's own length)

children.label: Match Disc Radius
children.name: Match Disc Radius
children.desc: Take the tube's base radius straight from Disc Radius, so the tube meets the disc rim seamlessly and the whole flower resizes off one master dimension. Only the BASE is linked -- the Tube Profile curve still shapes the radius from there up, so a funnel or bell still flares. Untick to set it independently

children.label: Radius
children.name: Radius
children.desc: Radius of the corolla tube at its base, independent of Disc Radius

children.label: Noise
children.name: Noise
children.desc: Irregularity along the tube's length -- a slow wobble in its radius, so it doesn't read as a machined extrusion. Rerolls with the flower's Seed, so a field of one species varies instead of repeating a single silhouette. The base is left untouched, so this can't reopen the join with the disc

children.label: Tube Resolution
children.name: Tube Resolution
children.desc: Points along the tube's own profile (more = smoother curvature)

children.label: Sides
children.name: Sides
children.desc: Points around the tube (with Fuse To Tube on, set by the petals instead)

children.label: Bud Length
children.name: Bud Length
children.desc: The tube's length in bud, as a fraction of its open Length -- it grows to full length over the Bloom slider. 1 keeps it the same at every Bloom

children.label: Bud Flare
children.name: Bud Flare
children.desc: How much of the Tube Profile's widening the tube has in bud: 0 a straight tube at the base radius, 1 the full open shape -- it swells into it over the Bloom slider. The base keeps its radius, so the disc and receptacle stay matched

children.label: Match Tube Angle
children.name: Match Tube Angle
children.desc: Start the petals off at the angle of the tube's own mouth, so they read as a continuation of the wall instead of straps attached at an unrelated tilt -- and so reshaping the top of the Tube Profile carries the petals with it. Pitch (under Shape) becomes an offset from that angle rather than an absolute tilt while this is on

children.label: Fuse Petals To Tube
children.name: Fuse Petals To Tube
children.desc: Widen each petal's base until they tile the tube's mouth exactly, closing the gaps between them so the corolla reads as one piece rather than separate lobes stuck to a cylinder. Fades back into the petal's own outline just above the mouth, so it doesn't override the Petal Shape

children.label: Flip Normals
children.name: Flip Normals
children.desc: Turn the corolla tube's faces the other way round (the front becomes the back)

children.label: Enable
children.name: Enable
children.desc: Generate a calyx (sepal whorl) beneath the petals

children.label: Resolution
children.name: Resolution
children.desc: Points along each sepal's spine

children.label: Width Resolution
children.name: Width Resolution
children.desc: Points across each sepal (Resolution is along it). With Fuse To Tube on, the tube is revolved with Count x (this - 1) sides to weld to it

children.label: Flip Normals
children.name: Flip Normals
children.desc: Turn the sepals' faces the other way round (the front becomes the back)

children.label: Length
children.name: Length
children.desc: Sepal length from its base to its tip

children.label: Width
children.name: Width
children.desc: Full sepal width at the Width Profile curve's peak

children.label: Top Shape
children.name: Top Shape
children.desc: Mirrors Petals' own Top Shape

children.label: Bottom Shape
children.name: Bottom Shape
children.desc: Mirrors Petals' own Bottom Shape

children.label: Cup
children.name: Cup
children.desc: Mirrors Petals' own Cup

children.label: Scale
children.name: Scale
children.desc: Overall size multiplier (scales Length and Width together), shaped across layers by its own Age Profile curve

children.label: Count
children.name: Count
children.desc: Number of sepals per layer, evenly spaced around the disc

children.label: Radial Offset
children.name: Radial Offset
children.desc: Signed distance moving each sepal's BASE along the disc's own radius, same convention as Petals' own Radial Offset

children.label: Vertical Offset
children.name: Vertical Offset
children.desc: Mirrors Petals' own Vertical Offset -- see its docstring

children.label: Azimuth Offset
children.name: Azimuth Offset
children.desc: One-time rotation of the WHOLE sepal ring relative to the petal ring -- defaults to alternating with a 5-petal flower (sepals peeking out between petals, not directly behind them)

children.label: Ring Height
children.name: Ring Height
children.desc: Signed distance seating the whole sepal ring below (-) or above (+) the petal attachment plane (each sepal's own base: Vertical Offset)

children.label: Spread Horizontal
children.name: Spread Horizontal
children.desc: Random scatter of each sepal's BASE azimuth around its ideal evenly-spaced ring position

children.label: Clamp Overlap
children.name: Clamp Overlap

children.label: Layers
children.name: Layers
children.desc: Number of stacked sepal rings (whorls), each offset up/down by Spacing and rotated by Spiral from the last

children.label: Spacing
children.name: Spacing
children.desc: Vertical distance between successive sepal layers -- typically well under 1mm

children.label: Spiral
children.name: Spiral
children.desc: Azimuthal rotation applied to each successive sepal layer, so layers interleave instead of stacking directly on top of each other. Defaults to the golden angle (~137.5°)

children.label: Gravity
children.name: Gravity
children.desc: Bends each sepal toward world-up (+) or world-down (-), shaped by the Gravity profile curve

children.label: Twist
children.name: Twist
children.desc: Total rotation of the sepal's cross-section around its own spine, shaped by the Twist profile curve

children.label: Up/Down
children.name: Curl Up/Down
children.desc: Steady bend up (+) or down (-) out of the flat disc plane, shaped along the sepal by its own profile curve

children.label: Left/Right
children.name: Curl Left/Right
children.desc: Steady sideways bend, curving the sepal into a sickle/scimitar shape as it extends outward

children.label: Out/In
children.name: Curl Out/In

children.label: Roll

children.label: Yaw

children.label: Pitch

children.label: Roll

children.label: Curl Up/Down

Keep growth out of this sphere entirely. Tips lean away as they approach and any that still reach the boundary stop there, the same way they stop at a wall
Aim growth at this point from anywhere, with no falloff. A training goal for a whole plant rather than a local magnet - Radius is ignored
Grow in the plane this effector faces, for an espalier or a fan. Rotate the effector to turn the plane. Radius is how far either side of the plane the flattening reaches

Spiral growth around this effector's axis, for a stem twining up a pole. Rotate the effector to aim the axis. Radius is how far out from the axis it reaches. Pair it with an Attract on the same spot to keep the stem against the pole

Turn each node's frame to face this effector, so the leaves and flowers on it swing round - put one where the sun is and the foliage follows. It turns where branches leave the stem too, so on a bushy plant the whole shape shifts, not just the foliage. Turn each node's frame to lie flat in this effector's plane. Same reach as Align Up - foliage and branch angles both. Rotate the effector to turn the plane

Different from an indeterminate plant with nothing to flower with: those stems never stop, and grow on until the plant runs out of developmental span
One flower at the tip of each stem
Flowers on short pedicels along a continuing tip (foxglove, delphinium)
Like a raceme but the flowers sit directly on the stem, no pedicels (plantain, many grasses)
A raceme whose lower pedicels are longer, bringing every flower up to about one level (yarrow)
Every pedicel radiating from one point at the tip, filling a dome right through its centre (allium)
An umbel whose pedicels are solved to land on one plane, so the head reads flat (cow parsley, Orlaya)

The stems bear no flowers themselves and hang catkins at their nodes instead - hazel, birch, willow. The one type here that is not something a stem turns into at its tip: a hazel's twigs go on being twigs and carry catkins along their length, on short stalks.

Shape them in the Catkins box below. They are modelled rather than instanced, so they hang under their own weight and need no asset assigned

A branched raceme: the stem carries branches rather than flowers and does not flower itself, and each branch repeats that until the last one, which flowers (oat, astilbe, yucca). Its depth is Branching Depth below, counted inside the inflorescence and independent of Max Branch Order - so a tree can carry panicles on twigs that are already several branch orders deep

Rings of flowers spaced up the stem, each subtended by a pair of leafy bracts, with bare stem between them - the false whorl of the mint family (dead-nettle, motherwort, mint, salvia). Sets Flowers per Whorl and Bract Size, which are ordinary controls the other flowering kinds can use too. Botanically each ring is two condensed cymes rather than a true whorl; this builds a real ring, which reads the same at mint density

The tip flowers first and stops, and growth carries on from shoots just below it, each repeating the pattern. This is the unstamped form: set Relays per Node and Relay Rotation yourself. The four named cymes below - Scorpioid, Helicoid, Dichasium, Pleiochasium - are this same mechanism with those two numbers already set, and are what you want unless you are after a combination they do not name

A zigzag chain: the tip flowers and one shoot below it carries on, alternating sides each time, so the whole spray kinks from side to side in one plane (forget-me-not, comfrey, heliotrope). Sets Relays per Node to 1 and Relay Rotation to 180. How hard it zigzags is Branch Angle in the Branching box - +90 grows straight on with no kink, lower values fork harder every relay

Like a scorpioid cyme but every relay arises on the same side rather than alternating, so instead of zigzagging the spray coils (Alstroemeria, sundew, many nightshades). Sets Relays per Node to 1 and Relay Rotation to 0 - that single number is the whole difference between this and a scorpioid cyme

The familiar forked cyme: the spent tip is flanked by two shoots, each of which forks again, doubling every generation (chickweed, campion, most pinks). Sets Relays per Node to 2 and Relay Rotation to 90, so successive forks cross rather than stacking in one plane. Note the count doubles per Branching Depth

Three or more shoots in a whorl below each spent tip, giving a broad umbel-like spray (spurge). Sets Relays per Node to 3 and Relay Rotation to 60. The count multiplies by Relays per Node every Branching Depth, so it grows very fast - three at depth 3 is 27 flowers

A spike of spikes: every node of the flowering stem carries a whole spike of its own instead of one flower. Sets Type to Spike and Branching Depth to 1 - the dropdown then reads Spike, because that is what this is

A corymb whose flowers are themselves corymbs, so the head reads as a broad flat spray of little flat sprays (elder, yarrow). Sets Type to Corymb, Branching Depth to 1, and the Branching box - branches short, well spaced, finely tapered and arched
An umbel of umbels: each ray of the head ends in a whole umbel of its own. Sets Type to Umbel, Branching Depth to 1 and a long branch length, so the umbellets stand clear of one another

The cow parsley and hogweed form: rays from one point, each ending in its own flat-topped umbel. Sets Type to Flat Umbel, Branching Depth to 1, and the Branching box - ten long, slender, gently arched rays

children.label: Attachment Location
children.name: Attachment Location
children.desc: Where the inflorescences arise - at the tips of stems, along them, out of old wood, or from the base of the plant
items: Each stem finishes by becoming the inflorescence - the usual case, and what a foxglove, a yarrow or an allium does

Inflorescences arise at nodes along the stems, each on its own short stalk, while the stems go on being stems and bear no flowers themselves. Wisteria, laburnum, birch and hazel.

The stalks are not branches: they carry no leaves and sit outside Branch Density and Branching Zone, so those keep describing the plant's woody shape. Pair with Orientation to make them hang
From partway along an internode rather than at a node. Uncommon, but real - and the position along the internode is settable below

At a node, but on the far side of the stem from the leaf rather than in its axil - oppositifolious, as grapes and pepper are.

Half a turn round from where an axillary one would sit; everything else about it matches Axillary

Straight out of wood laid down seasons earlier on the TRUNK, well below the leaves - cauliflory, as figs and cacao do.

Defined by age rather than position: nothing appears until a node has carried for the stated number of steps, so a young plant shows none

The same old-wood break as Cauliflorous, but along the BRANCHES instead of the trunk - ramiflory, as redbud does on bare limbs.

Shares the Wood Age gate; the two differ only in which stems may bear it

From the root crown, straight out of the ground rather than from anywhere up a stem - violets, many bulbs, and a primrose's scapes.

Arises at once rather than waiting on Wood Age: a basal scape is the first thing such a plant does

From old wood that never carried a meristem at all - scattered between the nodes, following no phyllotaxis.

The one position whose buds are made rather than found, which is what makes it adventitious. Shares the Wood Age gate; use Per Node to set how many break from each internode

children.label: Per Node
children.name: Per Node
children.desc:
How many inflorescences arise at each position the attachment picks - 1 is a single one, higher fans a cluster out from the same point.

This is what a 'terminal cluster' or an 'axillary cluster' is: a count applied to a position, not a position of its own. As one control it clusters any attachment, including ones a fixed pair of cluster entries could never have covered

children.label: Orientation
children.name: Orientation
children.desc: Which direction this inflorescence prefers to point
items:
Prefer to lie along the stem that carries it, whatever that stem is doing.

Re-read as the plant grows, so the inflorescence swings when the branch bends. At Strength 0 this is simply the angle it left the stem at, which is what every plant did before orientation existed
Prefer to point up, against gravity

Prefer to lie level, perpendicular to gravity.

Level is a whole plane, so it keeps the compass direction the bud already had - radially out from its own stem - rather than sending every inflorescence to one side of the plant
Prefer the angle set below, measured from the parent stem's own direction rather than from world vertical - so it is stated relative to the stem and swings with it

children.label: Strength
children.name: Strength
children.desc:
How far the inflorescence is pulled from the direction it would naturally leave the stem at, toward the preferred direction above.

0 leaves it exactly as it grew; 1 pulls it fully onto the preference. It is a preference rather than a rule - even at 1 the result keeps some of where it came from, and the stem's own weight then bends it further, so an organ is not forced onto exact vertical.

It also sets how sharply the turn happens: the turn is always spread over the same short run of nodes, so a bigger pull bends harder over that run. Higher is sharper, and no value gives a hard corner

children.label: Reach It As Flowers Open
children.name: Reach It As Flowers Open
children.desc:
Arrive at the preferred direction as the inflorescence fills with flowers, rather than over its first few nodes - upright while it is a bud, bowed over once laden.

Different from Droop, which bends the finished stem: this moves while the inflorescence is still growing, so it changes where the flowers are actually placed

children.label: Depth
children.name: Branching Depth
children.desc:
Makes the inflorescence COMPOUND. At each place it would have put a flower it puts a whole inflorescence of its own kind instead, this many times over. 0 is simple.

1 turns a raceme into a panicle, an umbel into a compound umbel (carrot, cow parsley), a corymb into a compound corymb (yarrow, elder) and a spike into a compound spike (wheat). 2 gives the triple umbels real cow parsley makes. On a cyme it is instead how many times the tip relays, so a long zigzag chain wants 8 or more.

Independent of the Branching levels, which stay the plant's own vegetative branching - a plant can have several levels of branch under two of inflorescence, and one number cannot say both.

Watch the count: every level multiplies it by Rays (or by Relays per Node on a cyme), and it multiplies again by however many branch tips the plant itself has. Depth 2 on a bushy plant is thousands of flowers

children.label: Count
children.name: Branch Count
children.desc: How many branches the main stem of the inflorescence carries. Separate from Flower Count, which is how many flowers each of those branches ends up with - one number used to serve both, so ten branches of three flowers was not expressible. Only used by Panicle

children.label: Angle
children.name: Branch Angle
children.desc:
Which way an inflorescence branch leaves the main stem, measured from perpendicular: 0 is straight out sideways, +90 flat up along the stem, -90 flat down. Separate from the plant's own Branch Angle, which describes its woody branches. This is the main thing separating a diffuse, open panicle from a contracted, spike-like one.

On a cyme this is the zigzag: it is the angle each relay leaves the spent tip above it at, so +90 carries straight on with no visible kink and lower values fork harder every generation. The kink is exactly 90 minus this

children.label: Spacing
children.name: Branch Spacing
children.desc: Gap between successive branches along the main stem of the inflorescence, relative to an ordinary internode. Separate from Flower Spacing on purpose: a panicle stands its branches well apart while crowding the flowers on them, and one number cannot say both. Only used by Panicle

children.label: Nodes
children.name: Branch Nodes
children.desc: Nodes an inflorescence branch lays down before it starts flowering - the bare basal stretch of a panicle branch. Only used by Panicle

children.label: Length
children.name: Branch Length
children.desc: How far apart the nodes of an inflorescence branch sit, and so how long the branch is. Separate from Branch Nodes, which is how many flowers it carries - before this a branch could only be lengthened by making it carry more. Only used by Panicle

children.label: Width
children.name: Branch Width
children.desc: A branch's thickness where it leaves the main stem, as a fraction of that stem's own thickness there - so 1.0 is exactly as thick as the stem it comes off, and it cannot go above that. Same as Pedicel Width. Its graph is the taper along one branch, base to tip, and shapes only the taper - the base width is this number's to set. Thinner branches also arch further, because bending resists as the fourth power of radius. Only used by Panicle

children.label: Bend
children.name: Branch Bend
children.desc: A steady arch along each inflorescence branch, held in the branch's own plane - so it turns with the branch rather than always heading for the ground. 1 is a quarter turn from base to tip. This is shape; Branch Droop below is weight. Only used by Panicle

children.label: Droop
children.name: Branch Droop
children.desc:
How far an inflorescence branch turns out of the way it was aimed, over its whole length. Negative sags it toward the ground, -1 hanging straight down; positive lifts it toward vertical - the same sign as Angle and Bend above it, and what an erect panicle's upswept primaries need.

Distinct from Peduncle Droop, which only bends the stretch below the lowest flower and therefore cannot touch a branch that carries branches rather than flowers. Unlike Bend it is measured against gravity, so it does not turn with the branch

children.label: Count
children.name: Flower Count
children.desc: Flowers per inflorescence. Ignored by Solitary and by the cymose kinds, which get their count from how many times they relay instead - that is Branching Depth times Relays per Node

children.label: Per Whorl
children.name: Flowers per Whorl
children.desc:
How many flowers each node of the inflorescence carries, in a ring around the stem. 0 follows the plant's own leaf arrangement, which is one flower per leaf position - so 0 is exactly what every kind did before this existed.

Separate from Trunk Pattern on purpose: one flower is placed per leaf position, so asking for a six-flowered whorl through the phyllotaxis also gives the leafy stem below six leaves per node. A mint has two. This is the flowering region stating its own arrangement

children.label: Spiral
children.name: Spiral
children.desc: The flowers' own spiral up the inflorescence: each flowering node's flower turned this many degrees round the stem from the last (137.5 is the golden angle). 0 follows the plant's leaf arrangement. Lets a spike spiral while its leaves stay two-ranked, as a grass's do. Flowers per Whorl (2 or more) replaces it

children.label: Spacing
children.name: Flower Spacing
children.desc: Spacing between flowers along the axis, relative to the leafy stem's own internode length. Below 1 packs the flowering region tighter than the stem below it, which is how most inflorescences sit

children.label: Spacing Base
children.name: Spacing Base
children.desc: The inflorescence's spacing base: the distance between flowers is this times Flower Spacing (Branch Spacing on a branched rachis), the same on every stem and branch. Stem and branch internodes are the Branching levels' Length instead

children.label: Weight
children.name: Flower Weight
children.desc: How heavy a full-size flower or head is. This is now the main thing that nods a blooming tip: a heavy head on a thin stem hangs, a light one stands up. Flower mass grows with the CUBE of Flower Size, so doubling a head's size makes it eight times heavier - size and weight together decide the droop

children.label: Young Size
children.name: Young Size
children.desc: How big an inflorescence is the moment it is laid down, as a share of mature - its flower spacing, flower size and pedicel length and width all start here and grow to full as it develops. Only the youngest racemes (started near the end of the season) show it; a mature one is always full size. The curve beside it shapes the growth from this start to full

children.label: Spread
children.name: Spread
children.desc: How much of the stem's circumference the flowers occupy. 360 is the full circle the leaf arrangement already gives; narrow it to crowd them onto one side, the way a foxglove does, and 0 puts every flower on a single line

children.label: Heliotropism
children.name: Flower Heliotropism
children.desc: How far each flower turns its face toward the Sun Object, after growth. The nodding-sunflower case: the stem stays where gravity left it, the head turns up to the sun and its own stalk curves with it (a stalk a branch leaves stays straight); 0 is off

children.label: Width
children.name: Pedicel Width
children.desc: How thick each pedicel is where it leaves the stem, as a fraction of the stem's own thickness there. 1 continues the stem's width, which reads as a short branch; most plants carry conspicuously finer pedicels than that

children.label: Bend
children.name: Pedicel Bend
children.desc: How strongly each pedicel curves. 0 gives straight spokes; higher makes it leave the stem sideways and turn up harder on its way to the flower, the way a real corymb does. A pedicel never swings wider than its own flower. This is shape only and does NOT move the flower - the pedicel arcs between the same two endpoints, so Length and Angle still decide where the flower sits

children.label: Length
children.name: Pedicel Length
children.desc: Length of the pedicel - the little stalk between the stem and each flower. A corymb lengthens the lower ones automatically; a spike and a catkin ignore this, because their flowers are sessile and have no pedicel at all

children.label: Angle
children.name: Pedicel Angle
children.desc: How far a pedicel tilts off horizontal. 0 leaves the stem straight out sideways, positive swings it up toward the tip, negative hangs it down for a drooping raceme. Plus or minus 90 presses it flat against the stem

children.label: Order
children.name: Bloom Order
children.desc: Which flowers open first. Later ones are still opening, so they read smaller and tighter
items: Lowest flowers open first and are furthest along
Outer flowers open first, working inward
Central flowers open first, working outward

children.label: Smooth bloom stage blending
children.name: Smooth bloom stage blending
children.desc: Blend smoothly between neighbouring bloom stages instead of snapping from one to the next. Every stage must have identical topology - stages baked from one flower do; a set of separately modelled flowers will not, and will scramble

children.label: Bloom
children.name: Bloom
children.desc: Where each flower's openness comes from
items: Flowers open as the plant matures: Progress is worked out from Age and the point in its life this species starts flowering. Scrub Age and the plant grows and blooms together
Progress is the slider below, independent of Age. This is the one to keyframe when the bloom needs its own timing
No timeline at all: each flower shows the stage its own bloom order calls for, so the first to open is out and the last is a bud

children.label: Spread
children.name: Bloom Spread
children.desc: How staggered the opening is. 0 opens every flower in lockstep; 1 means the last flower in the bloom order does not begin until Progress reaches 1, so the opening travels up the inflorescence as a wave. Under From Age the stagger already comes from when each flower was actually born, so this reads instead as how quickly a flower opens once it appears - higher leaves fewer buds at the tip

One row per filter on a component: a colour swatch, the attribute it reads, an invert marker, a per-attribute preview eye, and a mute. The window is tuned in the details below -- the row stays a legible summary. `data` is the component PG (only the active component's filters are drawn), reaching the growth PG through the object it lives on.

children.label: Add Property
children.desc: Add a property column: each mesh's preference for where it is high or low

children.label: Weights Only
children.desc: One row per mesh of the component's collection: new meshes get Weight 1, rows of meshes no longer in it go

children.label: Gravitropism
children.name: Gravitropism
children.desc: How strongly a stem corrects back toward the angle it is trying to hold. Higher makes stems stiff and true; lower lets them wander

children.label: Autotropism
children.name: Autotropism
children.desc: How much older stem straightens back to true as it ages, so the wander stays a live nodding tip on a tidy stem instead of a wobble all the way down. Higher keeps a shorter, tidier live zone at the very tip. 0 is off

children.label: Circumnutation
children.name: Circumnutation
children.desc: How far the growing tip nods off-axis each step in a coiling, helical sweep -- the spiralling seen in growth timelapses. Unlike Irregularity, which wanders at random, this winds a coherent helix. Its size is fought by Gravitropism, so raise Autotropism to see it on an upright plant. 0 is off

children.label: Circumnutation Rate
children.name: Circumnutation Rate
children.desc: How far the nod turns around the stem each step -- the pitch of the helix, its sign the handedness (left- vs right-winding). Does nothing while Circumnutation is 0

children.label: Internode Elongation
children.name: Internode Elongation
children.desc: How each internode stretches to its full length after it forms. Picking one sets the Internode Elongation curve and Duration; edit either and it reads Custom
items: Each internode reaches its full length before the next one forms -- one stretching at a time
Several internodes stretch at once: the lower ones keep growing for a while after new ones form above (most herbs)
A new internode stays short while the next nodes form, then stretches -- compressed young growth that spreads out later

children.label: Duration
children.name: Elongation Duration
children.desc: Growth steps an internode takes to reach its full length after it forms (one node forms per step): 1 = done before the next forms, higher = several stretching at once

children.label: Leaf Expansion
children.name: Leaf Expansion Duration
children.desc: Growth steps a leaf takes to grow from a tiny primordium to its full size, along the Leaf Expansion curve -- longer keeps young leaves small for longer

children.label: Preset
children.name: Preset
children.desc: A named starting point for the physical controls below. Picking one stamps its stiffness, variance, leaf and flower weight and stiffness curve, then snaps back to Custom - so the dropdown never claims a preset you have since edited
items: Soft, lax stem with a gently softening tip
Very flexible, a vine or scrambler
Soft tissue but heavy - a fleshy stem
Young wood, stiff but still bends
Rigid base, soft tip - the lamppost / weeping habit

children.label: Prune Limbs
children.desc: Draw a labelled glyph for every node, bud, apex, leaf and flower, and read one by pointing at it. P pins a card, X prunes the limb. Click again to turn off

children.label: Keep Dead Wood
children.name: Prune Keeps Dead Wood
children.desc: Whether a pruned limb stays as grey dead wood, or is removed entirely (the default). Distinct from the Age/Shade default, which keeps dead wood standing -- pruning is a gardener's cut, so it removes by default

children.label: Clear Pruning
children.desc: Restore every pruned limb on this plant

children.label: Smoothness
children.name: Smoothness
children.desc: How densely rings are placed along the stems. The stem is a smooth curve through every node; at 4 its faces are close to square, so bends read round and the welded junctions shade cleanly. Higher costs geometry

children.label: Weld Junctions
children.name: Weld
children.desc: Merge every stem and branch into one watertight mesh, joined at the junctions, instead of separate tubes overlapping each other

children.label: Weld Range
children.name: Weld Range
children.desc: How round each weld is: the radius of the fillet that blends a branch into its parent, in branch radii (smaller in a shallow crotch). Small keeps the join tight; large blends it out over more of the stem. 0 leaves a hard crease

children.label: Light Stalks
children.name: Light Stalks
children.desc: Build pedicels with four sides, and give stems too thin to show bark fewer rings on their straight runs. For a plant with thousands of flowers. Branch welds and bends keep their density

children.label: Weld
children.desc: Weld the active plant's stems: every junction joined and filleted into one mesh, with UVs. Builds in the background -- keep working meanwhile. Changing parameters after welding will require rebuilding the welds

children.label: Light Seeking
children.name: Light Seeking
children.desc: How far growing tips turn toward the light each step. Applied after Gravitropism, so a shaded shoot leans out from under whatever is shading it even though gravity would hold it upright. 0 ignores light direction

children.label: Leaf Heliotropism
children.name: Leaf Heliotropism
children.desc: How far each leaf turns its blade to face the sun, after growth. Set Sun Object below to the thing to track. Unlike an Align Up effector this aims each blade at the sun rather than rotating the whole leaf set; 0 is off

children.label: Sun Object
children.name: Sun Object
children.desc: The object leaves turn to face, for Leaf Heliotropism (each flower component picks its own). They aim at wherever it sits relative to the plant, so move it to place the sun -- any object works (an empty, a lamp, a mesh). Empty means no heliotropism

children.label: Collection
children.name: obstacle_collection
children.desc: Objects this plant grows around. Any mesh will do, and closed shapes work best. They block growth and cast shade. Empty means nothing is in the way

children.label: Clearance
children.name: Clearance
children.desc: How far from a surface this plant keeps its growing tips. Tips curve away as they approach, and one that runs out of room stops there instead of growing through. 0 turns obstacle response off entirely

children.label: Object
children.name: Ground
children.desc: A terrain mesh the plant rests on: a stem that bends down to it lies along its surface instead of the flat ground at the plant's base. Only the bend reads it -- growth is not steered. Empty means flat ground

children.label: Collection
children.name: effector_collection
children.desc: Effector empties that steer this plant by hand - attract, repel, forbid or aim. Unlike Light and Obstacles there is nothing to enable first: an effector in this collection acts straight away. Empty means nothing steers it

children.label: Add Effector
children.desc: Add an effector at the 3D cursor that steers the active plant's growth, and link it to that plant

children.label: Shade Death
children.name: Shade Death
children.desc: After growth, each branch is judged by the light at its base; below this it dies and takes its subtree with it. 0 (default) never kills. The plant shades itself, so this works with no obstacle in the scene; add obstacles overhead to shade a lower crown. 1.0 kills anything out of full sky

children.label: Keep Dead Wood
children.name: Keep Dead Wood
children.desc: Whether a dead branch stays as grey dead wood, or is removed entirely. Its leaves and flowers are shed either way -- a dead branch is bare

children.label: Dead Colour
children.name: Dead Colour
children.desc: What dead tissue is tinted toward. A shader sampling the Color vertex attribute shows it in a render; the Senescence debug view shows it in the viewport regardless of material

children.label: Stems
children.name: Bone Angle
children.desc: How far this level's stems or branches may bend along one bone before the rig starts the next: straight runs share a bone, bends get more. 0 = a bone per node. Read when the rig is built

children.label: Branches 1
children.name: Bone Angle
children.desc: How far this level's stems or branches may bend along one bone before the rig starts the next: straight runs share a bone, bends get more. 0 = a bone per node. Read when the rig is built

children.label: Build Rig
children.desc: Build a skeletal rig for the plant as it stands: a bone chain down every stem and branch (straight runs share a bone -- each level's Bone Angle), a bone per leaf, bract, flower, bud and fruit, and the welded mesh skinned to it with smooth weights. The plant then shows the rig (Rig View). Rebuilding replaces the previous rig

children.label: Rig View
children.name: Rig View
children.desc: Show this plant as its baked rig -- the skinned mesh, posed and animated by the bones -- instead of the live build. Still the one object you select and edit; any edit that regrows drops back to the live plant and marks the rig out of date

children.label: Show Bones
children.name: Show Bones
children.desc: Draw the rig's bones over the plant in Rig View

children.label: Display
children.name: Bone Display
children.desc: How the rig's bones are drawn in the viewport. Display only -- the skeleton and an export are the same either way
items: Bones as thin lines -- the least clutter on a dense rig

children.label: Fast Preview
children.name: Fast Preview
children.desc: Play the rig fast in Rig View: only the stems deform, and every leaf and flower stays a GPU instance that follows its bone -- the same look, a fraction of the work per frame. Off: the full skinned mesh deforms (slow with many flowers). Falls back to the full mesh while Vertex Wind is on. The export always writes the full mesh

children.label: Export Rig
children.desc: Export the rig as a skeletal mesh -- the bones and the skinned mesh in their bind pose, with weights, UVs, materials and the vertex colours -- to FBX or USD (by the file's extension), the plant's root at the origin; and beside it <name>_wind.json, the simulation groups Unreal's Dynamic Wind imports (Import Dynamic Wind Data). Build Rig first

children.label: Export Nanite Assembly
children.desc: Export the rig as a skeletal-mesh Nanite Assembly (USD) for Unreal 5.7+ Nanite Foliage: the stems as a skinned base mesh, every leaf and flower that is one of its component's meshes as an instance of it, bound to its own bone; flowers on their bloom stage. Beside it <name>_wind.json for Dynamic Wind. Build Rig first

children.label: Bone Wind
children.name: Bone Wind
children.desc: An approximation of Unreal's wind, to preview in Blender: the rig's bones sway with the gusts, thin limp parts most, everything on them riding along. Nothing of it is exported -- Unreal simulates the real sway itself, from the wind groups Export Rig writes (made from the same stem flexibility this preview uses). Plays on the timeline in Rig View; needs a rig (Build Rig)

children.label: Strength
children.name: Bone Wind Strength
children.desc: How hard the preview wind pushes the bones. Preview only -- Unreal's wind strength comes from its own wind source in the level

children.label: Stiffness
children.name: Bone Stiffness
children.desc: Trims how far the preview bends -- higher sways less. Each bone's own give still comes from the stem's flexibility, so thin limp parts sway while thick ones barely move. Preview only -- it does not change what Unreal gets

children.label: Vertex Wind
children.name: Vertex Wind
children.desc: Flutter leaves and petals with a wave driven by the vertex colours (Red: still at the base, free at the tip; Green / Blue: each leaf and plant out of step). A viewport preview of what an engine's foliage material does at runtime from the same colours -- never exported or baked. Needs a rig (Build Rig)

children.label: Strength
children.name: Vertex Wind Strength
children.desc: How far leaf and petal tips flutter. Shares Direction, Gust Speed and Turbulence with Bone Wind

children.label: Direction
children.name: Wind Direction
children.desc: Preview wind heading in degrees (0-360) on the ground plane; gusts swirl around it. Preview only -- Unreal takes its wind direction from the level

children.label: Gust Scale
children.name: Gust Scale
children.desc: Gust spatial frequency -- higher gives smaller, tighter gusts

children.label: Gust Speed
children.name: Gust Speed
children.desc: How fast the gust field drifts and evolves over time

children.label: Turbulence
children.name: Turbulence
children.desc: Swirl amount -- curl-noise eddying added to the wind heading

children.label: Wind Seed
children.name: Wind Seed
children.desc: Randomizes the whole gust pattern -- each value is a wholly different field (and decorrelates this plant from others)

Which node up its own axis the organ sits at, 0 at the base to 1 at the tip
Position along the organ's own axis, 0 at the axis base to 1 at its tip

How deep inside a fork / inflorescence the organ sits, 0 on vegetative stem rising with each split
How shaded the organ is by the plant's own canopy, 0 in open sky to 1 fully shaded -- sampled from the self-shading light field, so a dense clump reads its shaded interior
A flower's place on the bloom order (flowers only)
Seeded per-organ noise, for scattered thinning
1 on a shoot's own tip bud (its apex), 0 on axillary buds and every other organ -- keep only tip buds, or invert to keep only side buds
One of this plant's own attributes (Mapping & Classification panel): a distance to an object, noise, or two channels combined
One of this plant's named classes (Mapping & Classification panel): 1 where that class's own mask stack keeps the point, 0 elsewhere -- build a class once, reuse and chain it
